summary.short: Replaces New York General Business Law Article 44-B (RAISE Act) with rules for frontier AI developers: publish safety frameworks and transparency reports, report critical safety incidents to a new DFS office, file disclosure statements, and face Attorney General civil penalties. Effective January 1, 2027.
summary.long: Replaces Article 44-B of the New York General Business Law, as added by a 2025 chapter, with the Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act. It covers frontier developers that trained a foundation model using more than 10^26 operations, and 'large frontier developers' that, with affiliates, had over $500 million in prior-year gross revenues. Large developers must publish and annually review a frontier AI framework, publish transparency reports before deploying new or substantially modified models, and make no materially false statements on catastrophic risk. All frontier developers must report critical safety incidents to a new office within the Department of Financial Services within 72 hours, or 24 hours where there is imminent risk of death or serious injury. Large developers must file a disclosure statement, renewed every two years, and pay assessments. The Attorney General may seek civil penalties of up to $1 million for a first violation and $3 million for later violations. The text creates no private right of action. Exemptions cover accredited New York colleges and universities doing academic research and the Empire AI consortium and institute. Effective January 1, 2027.

notes: Text is a bill (S. 8828) that repeals and re-enacts GBL Article 44-B as proposed in S. 6953-B and A. 6453-B; the 2025 chapter itself is not reproduced. Section 3 shows original effective-date wording in brackets beside the new text; the markup is not rendered as strikethrough in this document. Section 5 ties sections 1, 2 and 4 to the 2025 chapter's effective date, so the new article's start is not stated independently. The registry status 'adopted' is not shown in the document text. Section 1420(9)(a) prints the frontier model compute threshold as '10º26'. Economic Development Law section 361 and Public Officers Law Article 6 are cited but not reproduced.

enforcement.triggered_by: A large frontier developer fails to publish or transmit a compliant document required under this article, makes a statement in violation of § 1421(4), fails to report an incident as required by § 1422, or fails to comply with its own frontier AI framework.
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Civil penalty not to exceed one million dollars for a first violation and not to exceed three million dollars per subsequent violation, determined based on the severity of the violation.
enforcement.penalty_formula: Up to $1,000,000 for a first violation; up to $3,000,000 per subsequent violation; amount determined based on the severity of the violation.

enforcement.triggered_by: Any person develops, deploys or operates a large frontier model in part in New York without a current disclosure statement filed with the Office, submits false information in its disclosure, or fails to timely pay an assessment; the Office acts after notice and hearing.
enforcement.max_penalty_text: A civil penalty of one thousand dollars for each day the entity fails to file a disclosure as required or fails to correct false information, and an amount equal to the assessments owed.
enforcement.penalty_formula: $1,000 for each day the entity fails to file a disclosure or fails to correct false information; plus an amount equal to the assessments owed; imposed in addition to any other penalty or liability under this article.
enforcement.cure_period: None stated; penalties may be levied only after notice and hearing.
